dharana.numbering_edition: Jaideva Singh 1979 (dhāraṇā 1 = verse 24; dhāraṇā 82 = verses 105–106 and dhāraṇā 89 = verses 113–114, otherwise one verse each; dhāraṇā 112 = verse 137)
dharana.sanskrit_iast: kuhanena prayogeṇa sadya eva mṛgekṣaṇe | samudeti mahānando yena tattvaṃ prakāśate ||
dharana.sanskrit_source: GRETIL e-text, compared with Wallis's concordance, Pradīpaka and the Singh scan
dharana.rendering: O doe-eyed one, by the use of a trick (kuhana), great joy arises at once, and through it reality is revealed.
dharana.rendering_attribution: School paraphrase drawing on Jaideva Singh (1979), Christopher Wallis and Bettina Bäumer (as printed in Wallis's concordance); not a quotation.
dharana.commentary_note: Singh reads kuhana as a magical performance: the spectator's ordinary mind is lifted into mute wonder and joy, free of thought-constructs, and in that moment the nature of Bhairava is revealed; any awe-inspiring scene works the same way. Singh also reports Lakshmanjoo's reading of kuhana as tickling (the armpit), contemplating the essence of the joy that arises. Wallis: 'a trick'; Śivopādhyāya (as cited by Wallis) glosses the reality revealed as the thought-free state.
dharana.technique_name: Sudden Joy from a Trick or a Wonder
dharana.instruction: When something astonishes you, notice the instant thought stops and rest in it.

verification.notes: Door index = Singh dhāraṇā number, read directly in Singh's own headings and cross-checked against The Mystery Within's Singh-numbered list and Wallis's concordance. Caveat: Singh was read from an OCR scan, not a print copy in hand.

source_disagreements: kuhana: Singh reads 'magic / a magical performance' (wonder); Lakshmanjoo (via Singh) reads 'tickling the armpit'; Wallis 'a trick'. This door follows the wonder reading and records the others.

seat.label: Any steady, comfortable position (school addition)
seat.summary: Any steady, comfortable position: sitting on a chair, sitting on the floor with support under the hips, or lying on the back. Standing or walking slowly is also acceptable when that is easier. Choose the position in which the body needs the least effort.
seat.honesty: School addition. Verse 66 does not specify a body position. The seat is a convenience so the dharana can be practised; it is not part of the technique and makes no claim of tradition.

points: the trick or the astonishing moment
geometry.summary: Not a body shape. The map is one moment in time: the instant of surprise or wonder, when thought stops and joy rises.
geometry.svg_hint: a small burst shape on a timeline, with an open space at its centre
geometry.honesty: Geometry records the dharana's own map of attention, not a body shape. Locations marked 'commentarial' come from commentary, not from the verse.

reaction.name: Catch the wonder
reaction.summary: School metaphor only: surprise or wonder knocks thinking out for a moment, and that moment is noticed. Not a biochemical or medical claim.

breath.lands_in: wherever the breath naturally ends; this door places nothing on the breath
breath.cue: Natural breath. Count about four in and four out only if it helps you settle, then let the count go. No forced hold.
breath.honesty: The counts are an optional school pacing aid, not part of the verse. Hold is always 0: this school never adds a deliberate breath-hold.

orientation.cue: Turn toward the instant of surprise itself
orientation.gravity: Let the floor or chair carry the body completely; there is no posture to hold
orientation.gaze: Eyes open; this happens in ordinary life
orientation.degrees_hint: No angle target: the VBT gives no posture for this dharana

attention.primary: The instant of surprise, wonder or sudden joy
attention.secondary: The thought-free gap inside that instant

adiyogi.verse_paraphrase: O doe-eyed one, by the use of a trick (kuhana), great joy arises at once, and through it reality is revealed.
adiyogi.method_summary: When something astonishes you (a magic trick, a sudden beautiful sight, an unexpected laugh), notice the instant when thinking stops and joy rises. Turn attention to that instant itself and rest in it as long as it lasts.

honesty.disclosure: Door 043 follows Vijñāna Bhairava Tantra dharana 43 (verse 66) in Jaideva Singh's numbering. The door-to-dharana index is a School of 112 Doorways teaching device. Singh's sequence is one edition's count, not an ancient one-to-one canon. The seat, counts, reaction and beat scripts are school additions.
honesty.notes: pairing_type is school_device: the dharana is the content, while the door index, seat and pacing are the school's.

safety.pain_rule: Pain is information. Pause, regress, or exit. Never push through sharp pain.
safety.open_seat_alternate: This door needs no particular posture: sit on a chair, sit on the floor with support, or lie down. Eyes may stay open.
safety.contraindication_notes: General practice caution only; not medical advice. Use ordinary, harmless moments of wonder; nothing needs to be staged or done to anyone. If anything feels distressing (dizziness, agitation, strong emotion), stop, open the eyes and rest attention on the feet and the floor.
